top_band: terracotta/red-brown tiled roof slope from row 2 to row 43 (lightest ridge band at rows 3-9, sloping tiled planes down to the eave at row 43)
evidence: Reading down a central column: rows 2-43 show the foreshortened top slope of the tiled roof (42 rows tall, with a lighter ridge band at rows 3-9 and a distinct eave edge at rows 42-43). Directly below the overhanging eave, rows 44-45 have a darker shadow cast on the cream plaster wall, which continues down to the stone plinth at row 78 (35 rows of vertical south face). The door is recessed inside a stone frame with inner top/side shadow, and the chimney top shows its dark opening.

style.evidence: The roof uses 6 terracotta/brown shading steps with individual tile highlights and dark red-brown material outlines. The plaster walls have subtle multi-tone speckle grain rather than flat fills, and the stone base, wood door, and shuttered window have crisp multi-step shading matching the Beodeul house references.
